mcq.q: If y = x⁴ + 4x³ + 7x² − 7x + 5, then dy/dx at x = 1 is:
mcq.explain: Differentiate term by term with d/dx(xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹ (the constant vanishes): dy/dx = 4x³ + 12x² + 14x − 7. At x = 1 this is 23. Putting x = 1 into y itself gives 10, which is the height of the curve, not its slope.
mcq.fast: Power rule: bring the power down, reduce it by one, then substitute.

mcq.q: If y = 5x⁴ − 4x³ − 2x² + 2x − 4, then dy/dx at x = 1 is:
mcq.explain: Differentiate term by term with d/dx(xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹ (the constant vanishes): dy/dx = 20x³ − 12x² − 4x + 2. At x = 1 this is 6. Putting x = 1 into y itself gives -3, which is the height of the curve, not its slope.
mcq.fast: Power rule: bring the power down, reduce it by one, then substitute.

mcq.q: If y = (4x − 5)(4x² − 4), then dy/dx at x = 3 is:
mcq.explain: Product rule: d(uv)/dx = u′v + uv′ with u = 4x − 5 (u′ = 4) and v = 4x² − 4 (v′ = 8x). At x = 3: u = 7, v = 32, v′ = 24. So dy/dx = 4 × 32 + 7 × 24 = 296. Multiplying the two derivatives (u′v′) is wrong.
mcq.fast: Or expand the product into one polynomial first, then differentiate and substitute.

mcq.q: If y = (3x − 3)(2x² + 1), then dy/dx at x = 4 is:
mcq.explain: Product rule: d(uv)/dx = u′v + uv′ with u = 3x − 3 (u′ = 3) and v = 2x² + 1 (v′ = 4x). At x = 4: u = 9, v = 33, v′ = 16. So dy/dx = 3 × 33 + 9 × 16 = 243. Multiplying the two derivatives (u′v′) is wrong.
mcq.fast: Or expand the product into one polynomial first, then differentiate and substitute.

mcq.q: If y = (x + 3)/(x − 2), then dy/dx at x = -1 is:
mcq.explain: Quotient rule: d(u/v)/dx = (v·u′ − u·v′)/v². Here u′ = 1, v′ = 1, so the numerator is (x − 2)(1) − (x + 3)(1) = -5 (the x-terms cancel). Hence dy/dx = -5/(x − 2)²; at x = -1 the denominator is 9, giving -5/9. Reversing the order in the numerator flips the sign.
mcq.fast: For (ax + b)/(cx + d), dy/dx = (ad − bc)/(cx + d)² directly.

mcq.q: If y = (2x − 9)/(4x − 1), then dy/dx at x = 2 is:
mcq.explain: Quotient rule: d(u/v)/dx = (v·u′ − u·v′)/v². Here u′ = 2, v′ = 4, so the numerator is (4x − 1)(2) − (2x − 9)(4) = 34 (the x-terms cancel). Hence dy/dx = 34/(4x − 1)²; at x = 2 the denominator is 49, giving 34/49. Reversing the order in the numerator flips the sign.
mcq.fast: For (ax + b)/(cx + d), dy/dx = (ad − bc)/(cx + d)² directly.

mcq.q: If y = (x² + 1)³, then dy/dx at x = 2 is:
mcq.explain: Chain rule: dy/dx = n(inner)ⁿ⁻¹ × d(inner)/dx = 3(x² + 1)² × 2x. At x = 2 the inner function is 5, so dy/dx = 3 × 5² × 4 = 300. Forgetting to multiply by the derivative of the inner function (2x) gives 75.
mcq.fast: Outer derivative × inner derivative, then substitute.

mcq.q: If y = (2x² − 4)³, then dy/dx at x = 1 is:
mcq.explain: Chain rule: dy/dx = n(inner)ⁿ⁻¹ × d(inner)/dx = 3(2x² − 4)² × 4x. At x = 1 the inner function is -2, so dy/dx = 3 × -2² × 4 = 48. Forgetting to multiply by the derivative of the inner function (4x) gives 12.
mcq.fast: Outer derivative × inner derivative, then substitute.

mcq.q: If y = log (8x + 1) (natural log), then dy/dx at x = 2 is:
mcq.explain: d/dx[log u] = (1/u) × du/dx. With u = 8x + 1, du/dx = 8, so dy/dx = 8/(8x + 1). At x = 2: 8/17 = 8/17. Forgetting the factor du/dx = 8 gives 1/17.
mcq.fast: log of a linear function: derivative = (coefficient of x) ÷ (the linear expression).

mcq.q: If y = log (2x + 6) (natural log), then dy/dx at x = 5 is:
mcq.explain: d/dx[log u] = (1/u) × du/dx. With u = 2x + 6, du/dx = 2, so dy/dx = 2/(2x + 6). At x = 5: 2/16 = 1/8. Forgetting the factor du/dx = 2 gives 1/16.
mcq.fast: log of a linear function: derivative = (coefficient of x) ÷ (the linear expression).

mcq.q: If y = e^(2x) × (x + 7), then dy/dx at x = 0 is:
mcq.explain: Product rule with d/dx(e^(2x)) = 2e^(2x): dy/dx = 2e^(2x)(x + 7) + e^(2x) × 1 = e^(2x)[2(x + 7) + 1]. At x = 0, e⁰ = 1, so dy/dx = 2 × 7 + 1 = 15. Dropping the second term of the product rule gives 14.
mcq.fast: At x = 0 every e^(kx) is 1: just evaluate k(x + a) + 1.

mcq.q: If x² + y² = 289, then dy/dx at the point (8, 15) is:
mcq.explain: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, treating y as a function of x: 2x + 2y·dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = −x/y. At (8, 15): −(8)/(15) = -8/15. Forgetting the dy/dx attached to the y-term is the common implicit-differentiation error.
mcq.fast: For x² + y² = r², slope = −x/y at the point.

mcq.q: If x² + y² = 225, then dy/dx at the point (12, 9) is:
mcq.explain: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, treating y as a function of x: 2x + 2y·dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = −x/y. At (12, 9): −(12)/(9) = -4/3. Forgetting the dy/dx attached to the y-term is the common implicit-differentiation error.
mcq.fast: For x² + y² = r², slope = −x/y at the point.

mcq.q: If x = 4t² and y = 8t, then dy/dx at t = -3 is:
mcq.explain: For parametric equations, dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt). Here dy/dt = 8 and dx/dt = 8t, so dy/dx = 8/(8t) = 1/t. At t = -3: -1/3. Dividing the other way round gives t. This curve is the parabola y² = 16x written in parametric form.
mcq.fast: dy/dx = (dy/dt) ÷ (dx/dt) = 1/t for this standard parabola.

mcq.q: If x = 3t² and y = 6t, then dy/dx at t = -3 is:
mcq.explain: For parametric equations, dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt). Here dy/dt = 6 and dx/dt = 6t, so dy/dx = 6/(6t) = 1/t. At t = -3: -1/3. Dividing the other way round gives t. This curve is the parabola y² = 12x written in parametric form.
mcq.fast: dy/dx = (dy/dt) ÷ (dx/dt) = 1/t for this standard parabola.

mcq.q: If y = 4x⁴ − 6x³ + 2x² + 4x, then d²y/dx² at x = 2 is:
mcq.explain: Differentiate twice. dy/dx = 16x³ − 18x² + 4x + 4; d²y/dx² = 48x² − 36x + 4. At x = 2: 124. The second derivative measures how the slope changes; a positive value means the curve is bending upwards (a possible minimum).
mcq.topic: Second derivative and the gradient of a curve
mcq.fast: Differentiate twice term by term; linear and constant terms vanish in d²y/dx².

mcq.q: If y = 3x³ − 6x² − 2x − 6, then d²y/dx² at x = -1 is:
mcq.explain: Differentiate twice. dy/dx = 9x² − 12x − 2; d²y/dx² = 18x − 12. At x = -1: -30. The second derivative measures how the slope changes; a positive value means the curve is bending upwards (a possible minimum).
mcq.topic: Second derivative and the gradient of a curve
mcq.fast: Differentiate twice term by term; linear and constant terms vanish in d²y/dx².

mcq.q: The total cost function is C(x) = x³ − 7x² + 7x + 1113. The marginal cost when x = 35 units is:
mcq.explain: Marginal cost is the derivative of total cost: MC = dC/dx = 3x² − 14x + 7. At x = 35: MC = ₹3,192. The fixed cost 1,113 does not affect MC. Total cost ₹35,658 and average cost ₹1,018.8 are different ideas.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Differentiate C(x), drop the constant, substitute x.

mcq.q: The total cost function is C(x) = (1/3)x³ − 6x² + 53x + 378. The marginal cost when x = 15 units is:
mcq.explain: Marginal cost is the derivative of total cost: MC = dC/dx = x² − 12x + 53. At x = 15: MC = ₹98. The fixed cost 378 does not affect MC. Total cost ₹948 and average cost ₹63.2 are different ideas.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Differentiate C(x), drop the constant, substitute x.

mcq.q: Revenue R(x) = −(1/2)x² + 139x and cost C(x) = 12x + 1034. The output that maximises profit is:
mcq.explain: Profit P(x) = R − C = −(1/2)x² + 127x − 1034. Set dP/dx = 0: 127 − 1x = 0, so x = 127. d²P/dx² = −1 < 0 confirms a maximum (profit ₹7,030.5). Maximising revenue alone gives 139 units, ignoring cost.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Maximum profit where MR = MC: p − 2qx = r.

mcq.q: Revenue R(x) = −(1/2)x² + 209x and cost C(x) = 31x + 1852. The output that maximises profit is:
mcq.explain: Profit P(x) = R − C = −(1/2)x² + 178x − 1852. Set dP/dx = 0: 178 − 1x = 0, so x = 178. d²P/dx² = −1 < 0 confirms a maximum (profit ₹13,990). Maximising revenue alone gives 209 units, ignoring cost.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Maximum profit where MR = MC: p − 2qx = r.

mcq.q: Total cost C(x) = 3x² + 37x + 432. Average cost is minimum when output x =
mcq.explain: Average cost AC = C/x = 3x + 37 + 432/x. dAC/dx = 3 − 432/x² = 0 gives x² = 144, x = 12. The second derivative 2 × 432/x³ is positive, so it is a minimum (AC = ₹109). Minimising total cost instead would give x = 0.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Min AC at x = √(fixed cost ÷ coefficient of x²) = √(432/3).

mcq.q: Total cost C(x) = 5x² + 32x + 2000. Average cost is minimum when output x =
mcq.explain: Average cost AC = C/x = 5x + 32 + 2,000/x. dAC/dx = 5 − 2,000/x² = 0 gives x² = 400, x = 20. The second derivative 2 × 2,000/x³ is positive, so it is a minimum (AC = ₹232). Minimising total cost instead would give x = 0.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Min AC at x = √(fixed cost ÷ coefficient of x²) = √(2,000/5).

mcq.q: ∫ from -1 to 0 of (−x³ + 2x² + 1) dx =
mcq.explain: Integrate term by term with ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1): the antiderivative is −(1/4)x⁴ + (2/3)x³ + x. Evaluate at the upper limit minus the lower limit: [0] − [-23/12] = 23/12. Adding the two values, or differentiating instead of integrating, are the usual slips.
mcq.fast: Antiderivative at the top limit minus at the bottom limit; when the lower limit is 0 only the top limit matters.

mcq.q: ∫ from 2 to 5 of (5x² − x − 9) dx =
mcq.explain: Integrate term by term with ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1): the antiderivative is (5/3)x³ − (1/2)x² − 9x. Evaluate at the upper limit minus the lower limit: [905/6] − [-20/3] = 315/2. Adding the two values, or differentiating instead of integrating, are the usual slips.
mcq.fast: Antiderivative at the top limit minus at the bottom limit; when the lower limit is 0 only the top limit matters.

mcq.q: ∫ from -2 to 0 of (4x³ − 4x² + 2x − 8) dx =
mcq.explain: Integrate term by term with ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1): the antiderivative is x⁴ − (4/3)x³ + x² − 8x. Evaluate at the upper limit minus the lower limit: [0] − [140/3] = -140/3. Adding the two values, or differentiating instead of integrating, are the usual slips.
mcq.fast: Antiderivative at the top limit minus at the bottom limit; when the lower limit is 0 only the top limit matters.

mcq.q: Marginal cost is MC = 6x² + 19x + 39 and fixed cost is ₹2,090. The total cost of producing 36 units is:
mcq.explain: Total cost is the integral of MC plus the fixed cost (the constant of integration): C(x) = 2x³ + (19/2)x² + 39x + 2,090. At x = 36: C = ₹1,07,028 + ₹2,090 = ₹1,09,118. Leaving out the fixed cost gives only the variable cost.
mcq.topic: From marginal functions back to totals
mcq.fast: Integrate MC, put x = 36, then add the fixed cost.

mcq.q: Marginal cost is MC = 6x² + 9x + 151 and fixed cost is ₹4,439. The total cost of producing 7 units is:
mcq.explain: Total cost is the integral of MC plus the fixed cost (the constant of integration): C(x) = 2x³ + (9/2)x² + 151x + 4,439. At x = 7: C = ₹1,963.5 + ₹4,439 = ₹6,402.5. Leaving out the fixed cost gives only the variable cost.
mcq.topic: From marginal functions back to totals
mcq.fast: Integrate MC, put x = 7, then add the fixed cost.

mcq.q: ∫ from 0 to 2 of 4x(x² + 1)⁴ dx =
mcq.explain: Substitute t = x² + 1, so dt = 2x dx and 4x dx = 2 dt. The limits become t = 1 to t = 5. Integral = 2 × [t⁵/5] from 1 to 5 = 2 × (3125 − 1)/5 = 6248/5. Forgetting to change the lower limit gives a larger value.
mcq.fast: Spot f′(x)·[f(x)]ⁿ: the integral is [f(x)]ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1), scaled by the constant.

mcq.q: ∫ from 0 to 2 of 6x(x² + 1)⁴ dx =
mcq.explain: Substitute t = x² + 1, so dt = 2x dx and 6x dx = 3 dt. The limits become t = 1 to t = 5. Integral = 3 × [t⁵/5] from 1 to 5 = 3 × (3125 − 1)/5 = 9372/5. Forgetting to change the lower limit gives a larger value.
mcq.fast: Spot f′(x)·[f(x)]ⁿ: the integral is [f(x)]ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1), scaled by the constant.

mcq.q: A product sells at ₹724 per unit, the variable cost is ₹116 per unit and fixed costs are ₹37,088. The break-even output is:
mcq.explain: At break-even, revenue = total cost: 724x = 37,088 + 116x. So (724 − 116)x = 37,088 and x = 37,088/608 = 61 units. Each unit contributes ₹608 towards fixed costs; dividing by the price ignores variable cost.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Break-even units = fixed cost ÷ contribution per unit (price − variable cost).

mcq.q: A product sells at ₹356 per unit, the variable cost is ₹334 per unit and fixed costs are ₹1,61,678. The break-even output is:
mcq.explain: At break-even, revenue = total cost: 356x = 1,61,678 + 334x. So (356 − 334)x = 1,61,678 and x = 1,61,678/22 = 7,349 units. Each unit contributes ₹22 towards fixed costs; dividing by the price ignores variable cost.
mcq.topic: Applications: cost, revenue, profit, break-even and propensities
mcq.fast: Break-even units = fixed cost ÷ contribution per unit (price − variable cost).
